title: How the Browser Loads a Page

questions.prompt: What is the job of DNS during a page load?

options.text: Encrypt the connection between browser and server
Map the site's hostname to a numeric IP address
Compress the HTML before sending it

questions.explanation: DNS (Domain Name System) translates a hostname like shop.example.com into the IP address the browser actually connects to. If it isn't cached, that lookup costs a round trip.

questions.prompt: Order these steps of a first HTTPS request, from earliest to latest.

items.text: Send the HTTP request for the HTML

questions.explanation: The browser must resolve the name, open a TCP connection, negotiate TLS, send the request, and then wait for the first byte. Each handshake costs a round trip.

questions.prompt: The time from navigation start to the first byte of the response is called ____ (three-letter abbreviation).
questions.explanation: TTFB (Time to First Byte) measures the delay until the first response byte, including DNS, connection setup, TLS, server think time, and travel.

questions.prompt: Which of these are part of TTFB? Select all that apply.

options.text: Downloading every image on the page

questions.explanation: TTFB bundles redirects, DNS, TCP connect, TLS, server think time, and the first byte's travel. Downloading all images happens later and is not part of TTFB.

questions.prompt: Match each step to what it does.

pairs.right: Turn a hostname into an IP address
Open a reliable connection to the server
Set up HTTPS encryption and verify the certificate
Time until the first response byte arrives

questions.explanation: Each stage has a distinct job; the two handshakes each cost roughly one network round trip before your HTML can even be requested.

questions.prompt: Why does adding a new third-party origin (a different hostname) cost more than it first appears?

options.text: It always doubles your JavaScript size
The browser must do a fresh DNS lookup, TCP handshake, and TLS handshake for that origin before any of its bytes download
It disables HTTP caching for the whole page
It forces the page to reload from scratch

questions.explanation: Every brand-new origin pays its own DNS + TCP + TLS setup cost. That's why consolidating origins and using preconnect on the critical ones helps.
